name: Soho double-acting engine
summary: An 18-inch double-acting steam engine at Soho that used sun-and-planet gearing to turn a shaft, first driving a corn mill in 1783.
description: An 18-inch-cylinder, double-acting rotative engine using rack-and-sector connection and internal sun-and-planet gear, initially driving a corn mill.
tier_reason: A major reusable result, process or system within its field; broader multi-field or multi-generation dependence on this exact referent is not established.
why: Milling corn needed continuous rotary power rather than the up-and-down stroke of a pumping engine.

date.basis: The archive gives 1783 and reports inconsistent March/June evidence.

events.statement: The engine was initially used to drive a corn mill at Soho in 1783.
events.scope: 18-inch-cylinder double-acting engine with rack-and-sector and internal sun-and-planet gearing.
events.caveats: Sources cited by the archive disagree on the month and stroke; no customer sale or first market offer is inferred.

evidence.locator: MS 3147/5/1340, technical description and final paragraph
evidence.supports: Describes the 18-inch double-acting rack-and-sector engine with internal sun-and-planet gear driving a corn mill; records disagree on March/June 1783.

date.basis: First drawing dated August 1782; operation appears in a March 1783 diary reference, while the engine list gives first trial in June 1783.

events.statement: An 18-inch-cylinder, double-acting rotative engine using rack-and-sector connection and internal sun-and-planet gear, initially driving a corn mill.
events.caveats: Item-level catalogue inspected, not all drawings or diary leaves. The catalogue notes conflicting stroke lengths and first-operation records; no precise stroke or month is asserted.

evidence.locator: MS 3147/5/1340: technical specification; August 1782 first drawing; final paragraph
evidence.supports: Configuration, initial corn-mill duty and conflicting March/June 1783 operation evidence.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest defensible dated record of this scoped referent in the retained evidence; later community entry is recorded separately. community_entry.rationale: The named mill’s operation establishes actual use of this specific machine, rather than only the drawing or patent.
community_entry.caveats: Sources cited by the archive disagree on the month and stroke; no customer sale or first market offer is inferred.

caveats: Item-level catalogue inspected, not all drawings or diary leaves. The catalogue notes conflicting stroke lengths and first-operation records; no precise stroke or month is asserted.

links.statement: The Soho engine implemented Watt's double-acting arrangement with rack-and-sector transmission, combined with internal sun-and-planet gearing.
links.alternatives: The patent permits other piston-to-beam connections; later engines used parallel motion.
links.caveats: This does not assert that the Soho engine continuously used expansive cutoff.
links.timing: March/July 1782 specification precedes August 1782 drawings and 1783 operation.

evidence.locator: MS 3147/5/1340: technical specification and final paragraph
evidence.supports: Named engine, rack/sector, double action and Boulton & Watt development context.

links.statement: The Soho double-reciprocating engine used the internal sun-and-planet arrangement included in Watt's 1781 patent.
links.alternatives: Cranks and other reciprocating-to-rotary converters were available; patent constraints affected selection.
links.caveats: No inference that all rotary steam engines descended from this mechanism.
links.timing: Grant 1781 and enrollment February 1782 precede August 1782 drawings and 1783 use.

evidence.supports: Explicitly identifies the engine's internal sun-and-planet mechanism with Watt's 1781 patent.

evidence.locator: Section 23: Fifth Method, drawing No. 5 figures 3–4

links.statement: Were slide rules part of engine calculation at Soho? This would join calculating tools to steam.
links.caveats: Evidence needed: Soho or Watt papers documenting slide-rule use for engine work on this configuration.
links.finding: The two inspected records establish a calculating instrument and the particular Soho engine independently, but neither says the Soho engine was calculated or manufactured using Oughtred’s instrument. Chronology and plausible utility do not establish a link.
